intro: Causar means to cause or to bring about. It's a regular -ar verb, used a lot with problems, damage, delays and reactions: causar problemas, causar um acidente.

quick.en: I don't want to cause trouble.
It caused a lot of damage.

presente.en: I'm sorry if I cause any inconvenience.

presente.pt: Tu [causas] muitos problemas à tua irmã.
presente.en: You cause your sister a lot of problems.
Tobacco causes health problems.

presente.pt: Nós não [causamos] barulho depois das dez.
presente.en: We don't make noise after ten.

presente.pt: As obras [causam] muito trânsito na cidade.
presente.en: The roadworks cause a lot of traffic in the city.

perfeito.pt: [Causei] um pequeno acidente com o carro.
perfeito.en: I caused a small accident with the car.
You made a good impression at the dinner.
The rain caused train delays.

perfeito.pt: Os turistas [causaram] muito barulho ontem à noite.
perfeito.en: The tourists caused a lot of noise last night.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, eu [causava] sempre problemas na escola.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I always caused trouble at school.
The noise caused problems for the neighbours.
We used to cause a lot of chaos at parties.
The dogs used to frighten the children.

futuro.en: The strike will cause delays tomorrow.
These changes will cause problems.
We won't cause any trouble, I promise.
You will make a good impression.

condicional.en: That would cause a lot of problems.
I would never cause problems on purpose.
The works would cause a lot of noise.
You would cause confusion if you said that.

presente.en: Smoking causes many problems.
I don't want to cause problems.
The traffic is causing delays.
presente.pt: O trânsito está a causar atrasos.

perfeito.en: What caused the accident?
The rain caused delays.
We made a lot of noise.

imperfeito.en: The noise caused problems every night.
imperfeito.pt: O barulho causava problemas todas as noites.

imperfeito.en: That dog always caused trouble.
You always caused confusion.

futuro.en: This is going to cause problems.
The strike is going to cause delays.
It won't cause any damage.

condicional.en: That would cause an accident.
It would cause too much noise.
Would that cause problems?

notes.presente: Causar algo a alguém = to cause someone something: Isso causa-me problemas. In everyday speech you'll also hear provocar with the same meaning.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: causámos (Brazil: causamos). Causar boa impressão = to make a good impression.
notes.imperfeito: Use the imperfeito for something that caused problems repeatedly or over time: O barulho causava problemas (the noise kept causing problems).
notes.futuro: In everyday European Portuguese you'll more often hear ir + infinitivo: Isto vai causar problemas.

recap: A chuva causou atrasos, mas chegámos a tempo. (The rain caused delays, but we arrived on time.)

intro: Evitar means to avoid or to prevent. It's a regular -ar verb, and it's very useful for habits, traffic and problems: evitar o trânsito, evitar comer tarde.

presente.en: I avoid eating after ten.
You always avoid talking about that.

presente.pt: Ele [evita] o centro da cidade à hora de ponta.
presente.en: He avoids the city centre at rush hour.
We avoid sugar.
They avoid travelling in August.

perfeito.en: I avoided the traffic because I left early.
You avoided the question!
The driver avoided the accident.
We avoided the motorway.

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I avoided vegetables.
She always avoided the neighbours.
We used to avoid going out when it rained.
They used to avoid talking about politics.

futuro.en: I will avoid the same mistakes.
We will avoid the rush hour.
That way you'll avoid problems.
This solution will prevent delays.

condicional.en: I would avoid that restaurant.

condicional.pt: [Evitarias] muitos problemas se falasses com ele.
condicional.en: You would avoid a lot of problems if you talked to him.
That would avoid the traffic.
They would avoid the centre, if they could.

presente.en: I avoid coffee at night.
We try to avoid traffic.
Are you avoiding me?

perfeito.en: She avoided the question.
We avoided the motorway.
I avoided an accident.

imperfeito.en: He used to avoid sugar.
We used to avoid the city centre.
You always avoided the subject.

futuro.en: I'm going to avoid the same mistakes.
We are going to avoid the rush hour.
futuro.pt: Vamos evitar a hora de ponta.

futuro.en: Are you going to avoid sugar?

condicional.en: I would avoid that street.
That would avoid problems.
Would you avoid that?

notes.presente: Evitar takes a noun or an infinitive directly, with no preposition: evito comer tarde (I avoid eating late). The ongoing form uses estar a: Estás a evitar-me? (Are you avoiding me?)
notes.perfeito: European spelling: evitámos (Brazil: evitamos). Evitar can also mean to prevent: evitei um acidente (I prevented an accident).
notes.imperfeito: Evitei o trânsito = one occasion. Evitava o trânsito = I used to avoid it / I was avoiding it.
notes.futuro: In everyday speech: vou evitar, vamos evitar. The synthetic future (evitarei) sounds more formal.

compare.en: to run away from / to escape
compare.ex: Ele foge sempre das perguntas difíceis.

recap: Saí cedo para evitar o trânsito. (I left early to avoid the traffic.)

intro: Determinar means to determine, to establish or to set. It's a regular -ar verb and a bit formal; you'll see it in news, work and official contexts.

presente.en: The weather determines our plans.

presente.pt: Eu [determino] o horário da minha equipa.
presente.en: I set my team's schedule.
Do you set the price?
We set the rules at home.

presente.pt: Os médicos [determinam] a causa do problema.
presente.en: The doctors determine the cause of the problem.

perfeito.pt: Os médicos [determinaram] a causa da doença.
perfeito.en: The doctors determined the cause of the illness.

perfeito.pt: A polícia [determinou] a hora do acidente.
perfeito.en: The police determined the time of the accident.
We set the price together.
I set the rules of the game.

imperfeito.en: Money determined everything back then.

imperfeito.pt: Os pais [determinavam] a hora do jantar.
imperfeito.en: The parents decided dinner time.
I used to set the shop's opening hours.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [determinávamos] o menu da semana ao domingo.
imperfeito.en: We used to decide the week's menu on Sundays.

futuro.en: The result will determine the winner.
The tests will determine the cause.
We will set the date tomorrow.
I will set the price later.

condicional.en: That would determine the result.
I would set different rules.
The tests would identify the problem.
How would you set the price?

presente.en: The weather determines our plans.
presente.pt: O tempo determina os nossos planos.

presente.en: Who sets the price?
It's hard to determine.

perfeito.en: The doctor determined the cause.
We set the date.
They set the rules.

imperfeito.en: Money determined everything.
My father set the rules.
imperfeito.pt: O meu pai determinava as regras.

imperfeito.en: The weather determined our holidays.
imperfeito.pt: O tempo determinava as nossas férias.

futuro.en: The test is going to determine the result.
futuro.pt: O teste vai determinar o resultado.

futuro.en: We are going to set the date tomorrow.
Who is going to set the price?

condicional.en: That would determine everything.
How would you set the price?
The doctor would determine the cause.

notes.presente: Determinar is a bit formal. In everyday speech you'll often hear decidir (to decide) or definir (to set): definir a data. The adjective determinado means both 'determined' (uma pessoa determinada) and 'certain / specific' (num determinado dia).
notes.perfeito: European spelling: determinámos (Brazil: determinamos).
notes.imperfeito: Use the imperfeito for something that was generally true in the past: O dinheiro determinava tudo.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vamos determinar a data amanhã.

patterns.en: to be determined to do something

recap: O tempo determina os nossos planos para o fim de semana. (The weather determines our plans for the weekend.)

intro: Anunciar means to announce, and also to advertise. It's a regular -ar verb; you'll hear it at stations and airports and read it in the news.

quick.en: Have they announced the flight yet?
They're going to announce it tomorrow.

presente.en: I'll announce the news tomorrow.
Are you announcing the winner?
The company is announcing new jobs.
We'll announce the wedding on Sunday.

presente.pt: Eles [anunciam] os voos em português e em inglês.
presente.en: They announce the flights in Portuguese and in English.

perfeito.en: The government announced new measures.
They announced the train's delay.
We announced our engagement at dinner.
I announced the news to the family.

imperfeito.en: On the radio they always announced the weather.

imperfeito.pt: O jornal [anunciava] chuva para o fim de semana.
imperfeito.en: The newspaper was forecasting rain for the weekend.
I used to announce the games at school.
We used to advertise the parties at the café.

futuro.en: The president will announce the decision tomorrow.
They will announce the winner at eight.
I will announce the date soon.
We will announce the wedding in May.

condicional.en: I would announce the news later.
The company would never announce that.
When would you announce the news?

condicional.pt: Nós [anunciaríamos] a festa nas redes sociais.
condicional.en: We would announce the party on social media.

presente.en: They announce the flights in English.
presente.pt: Eles anunciam os voos em inglês.

presente.en: The company is announcing new jobs.
presente.pt: A empresa está a anunciar novos empregos.

presente.en: We announce the results today.

perfeito.en: They announced the delay.
She announced the news.
We announced the wedding.

imperfeito.en: The radio always announced the weather.
imperfeito.pt: A rádio anunciava sempre o tempo.

imperfeito.en: They used to announce the trains.
I used to announce the games at school.
imperfeito.pt: Eu anunciava os jogos na escola.

futuro.en: They are going to announce the winner.
I'm going to announce the date soon.
futuro.pt: Vou anunciar a data em breve.

futuro.en: When are they going to announce the results?

condicional.en: I would announce it later.
Would you announce the news today?
They would never announce that.

notes.presente: Watch the stress: eu anuncio (verb, stress on -ci-) vs o anúncio (noun: advertisement / announcement). The presente is often used for near-future plans: Anunciamos amanhã.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: anunciámos (Brazil: anunciamos).
notes.imperfeito: Anunciava can describe a forecast or something repeated: O jornal anunciava chuva (the paper was forecasting rain).
notes.futuro: Ir + infinitivo is the everyday choice: vão anunciar o vencedor. Anunciará sounds like the news.

compare.en: to warn / to let someone know

recap: Já anunciaram o nosso voo! (They've already announced our flight!)

intro: Exigir means to demand or to require. It's a regular -ir verb with one spelling change (eu exijo), used for people demanding things and for tasks that require time or effort.

presente.en: I demand an explanation!
You demand too much of yourself.
This job requires a lot of patience.
We demand respect.
Customers demand good service.

perfeito.pt: O cliente [exigiu] o dinheiro de volta.
perfeito.en: The customer demanded his money back.
I demanded to speak to the manager.
The workers demanded a pay rise.
We demanded a quick answer.

imperfeito.en: My teacher was very demanding.
My parents demanded good grades.
You never asked for anything.
At the beginning, we didn't demand anything.

futuro.en: The new job will require a lot of work.
The customers will demand an answer.
I will demand an explanation.
We will demand more safety.

condicional.en: I would demand my money back.
That would take a lot of time.
Would you demand the same?
They would never demand so much.

presente.en: I demand an explanation.
This job requires a lot of time.
The teacher demands a lot from the students.
presente.pt: A professora exige muito dos alunos.

perfeito.en: He demanded his money back.
perfeito.pt: Ele exigiu o dinheiro de volta.

perfeito.en: We demanded an answer.
I demanded to speak to the manager.

imperfeito.en: My parents demanded good grades.
imperfeito.pt: Os meus pais exigiam boas notas.

imperfeito.en: The boss was very demanding.
You never asked for anything.

futuro.en: The new job is going to require a lot of work.
futuro.pt: O novo emprego vai exigir muito trabalho.

futuro.en: They are going to demand a pay rise.
That is going to require patience.

condicional.en: I would demand an explanation.
That would take a lot of time.
Would you demand your money back?

notes.presente: Spelling change only: g becomes j before o, so eu exijo (to keep the soft sound). Every other form keeps the g: exiges, exige, exigimos. Exigente = demanding: um chefe exigente.
notes.perfeito: In -ir verbs, nós is the same in the presente and the perfeito: exigimos = we demand / we demanded. Context tells you which.
notes.imperfeito: Exigia describes a habit or general trait in the past: O meu professor exigia muito (my teacher was demanding).
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, isso vai exigir paciência.

patterns.en: to expect a lot from someone

recap: Aprender uma língua exige paciência, mas vale a pena. (Learning a language requires patience, but it's worth it.)

intro: Transformar means to transform or to turn something into something else. It's a regular -ar verb, usually followed by em: transformar a sala num escritório.

quick.en: I want to transform the garage.

presente.en: I turn old clothes into bags.
You turn everything into a party!

presente.pt: O frio [transforma] a água em gelo.
presente.en: The cold turns water into ice.

presente.pt: Nós [transformamos] a sala num escritório durante o dia.
presente.en: We turn the living room into an office during the day.

presente.pt: As crianças [transformam] a casa num caos.
presente.en: The children turn the house into chaos.

perfeito.en: The trip transformed my life.
They turned the garage into a gym.
We turned the bedroom into an office.
I transformed the garden in the summer.

imperfeito.en: Winter used to transform the village.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, eu [transformava] caixas em casas.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to turn boxes into houses.
They turned everything into a game.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [transformávamos] a sala numa pista de dança.
imperfeito.en: We used to turn the living room into a dance floor.

futuro.en: This project will transform the city.
The works will transform the neighbourhood.

futuro.pt: [Transformaremos] a cave numa sala de jogos.
futuro.en: We will turn the basement into a games room.
I will turn this room into an office.

condicional.en: I would transform the kitchen.
A child would transform our life.
How would you transform this space?

condicional.pt: Nós [transformaríamos] a casa toda, se tivéssemos dinheiro.
condicional.en: We would transform the whole house, if we had money.

presente.en: Heat turns ice into water.
presente.pt: O calor transforma o gelo em água.

presente.en: We are transforming the garage.
You turn everything into a problem.

perfeito.en: The trip transformed my life.
perfeito.pt: A viagem transformou a minha vida.

perfeito.en: We turned the room into an office.
The city changed a lot.

imperfeito.en: The children turned everything into a game.
imperfeito.pt: As crianças transformavam tudo num jogo.

imperfeito.en: Winter used to transform the village.
I used to turn boxes into houses.

futuro.en: This project is going to transform the city.
futuro.pt: Este projeto vai transformar a cidade.

futuro.en: We are going to transform the kitchen.
Are you going to transform the garden?

condicional.en: I would transform this room.
That would transform our life.
How would you transform the garden?

notes.presente: Transformar X em Y = to turn X into Y. Remember the contractions em + um = num, em + uma = numa: transformar a sala num escritório.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: transformámos. The reflexive transformar-se means to turn into / to become: Transformou-se num grande problema.
notes.imperfeito: Use the imperfeito for repeated changes in the past: Em criança, transformava caixas em casas.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vamos transformar a cozinha.

patterns.en: to make a problem out of everything

compare.ex: Mudei de casa no ano passado.

recap: Transformámos a garagem num pequeno escritório. (We turned the garage into a small office.)

intro: Vencer means to win, to beat or to overcome. It's a regular -er verb with one spelling change (eu venço). It sounds a bit stronger than ganhar and is common in sport and in vencer o medo (to overcome fear).

presente.pt: Eu [venço] sempre o meu irmão no xadrez.
presente.en: I always beat my brother at chess.
You always win at cards!
Who's winning today?
We almost always win at home.
They win every game.

perfeito.pt: O Porto [venceu] o jogo por dois a zero.
perfeito.en: Porto won the game two-nil.
We won the final!
They won the championship.
I finally overcame my fear of flying.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, eu [vencia] sempre às cartas.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I always won at cards.

imperfeito.pt: A nossa equipa [vencia] todos os anos.
imperfeito.en: Our team used to win every year.
We were winning until the last minute.
They always won at home.

futuro.en: They will win the next game.
Together we will win!
The best will win.
You will overcome your fear.

condicional.en: With more training, we would win.
He would win easily.
I would win if I had more time.
They would never win without the coach.

presente.en: Who's winning?
Our team always wins at home.
presente.pt: A nossa equipa vence sempre em casa.

presente.en: I always beat my brother at chess.
presente.pt: Venço sempre o meu irmão no xadrez.

perfeito.en: We won the game!
Who won?
She overcame her fear.

imperfeito.en: We were winning until the last minute.
They always won at home.
I always won at cards.

futuro.en: We are going to win!
Who is going to win the match?
The best one is going to win.

condicional.en: With more training, we would win.
Would they win without him?
I would win easily.

notes.presente: Spelling change only: c becomes ç before o, so eu venço (to keep the s sound). In everyday speech ganhar is more common for games: ganhar o jogo. Vencer is also used for deadlines and bills: o prazo vence amanhã (the deadline is tomorrow).
notes.perfeito: In -er verbs, nós is the same in the presente and the perfeito: vencemos = we win / we won.
notes.imperfeito: Vencíamos até ao último minuto = we were winning (background action) until something changed.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vamos vencer!

compare.ex: Ganhei o jogo e ganho bem no trabalho.

recap: Vencemos a final e festejámos a noite toda! (We won the final and celebrated all night!)

intro: Faltar means to be missing or lacking, and faltar a means to miss or skip (class, work). It's a regular -ar verb, often used in the 3rd person: falta sal, faltam dois dias.

presente.en: I never miss class.
You miss work a lot.
The soup needs salt.
We don't miss a single game.
There are two days left until Christmas.

perfeito.en: Yesterday I missed work.
Why did you miss the meeting?
There was a power cut during the night.
Three students were absent today.

imperfeito.en: Nothing was lacking in that house.
I never used to miss school.

imperfeito.pt: [Faltavam] cinco minutos para o fim do jogo.
imperfeito.en: There were five minutes left in the game.

imperfeito.pt: Às vezes, nós [faltávamos] às aulas de ginástica.
imperfeito.en: Sometimes we skipped PE classes.

futuro.en: I won't miss your party.
You won't lack anything.
We won't miss the wedding.

futuro.pt: Muitos alunos [faltarão] por causa da greve.
futuro.en: Many students will be absent because of the strike.

condicional.en: I would never miss your birthday.
Without you, something would be missing.

condicional.pt: Sem a greve, não [faltariam] tantos alunos.
condicional.en: Without the strike, so many students wouldn't be absent.
Would you skip work for a concert?

presente.en: There are two days left until the holidays.
presente.pt: Faltam dois dias para as férias.

presente.en: I don't have enough time.
What's missing?

perfeito.en: I missed work yesterday.
Why did you miss class?
There was a power cut.

imperfeito.en: Nothing was missing.
There were five minutes left.
He often missed school.

futuro.en: I'm not going to miss your party.
futuro.pt: Não vou faltar à tua festa.

futuro.en: You won't lack anything.
Are you going to miss the meeting?

condicional.en: I would never miss your birthday.
condicional.pt: Eu nunca faltaria ao teu aniversário.

condicional.en: Without you, something would be missing.
Would you skip work for a concert?
condicional.pt: Faltarias ao trabalho por um concerto?

notes.presente: Two uses. 1) Something is missing: the missing thing is the subject, so the verb agrees with it (falta sal, faltam dois dias); for the person who lacks it, use me/te/lhe: falta-me tempo. 2) Faltar a = to miss / skip: falto às aulas. To miss a person you love is ter saudades de, not faltar.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: faltámos. Faltou a luz / a água = there was a power cut / the water went off.
notes.imperfeito: Faltavam cinco minutos = there were five minutes left (background). Faltava muito à escola = he used to miss school a lot.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, não vou faltar à tua festa. After não the pronoun goes before the verb: não te vai faltar nada.

patterns.en: there are X days left until...
to have a power cut / no water

compare.en: to miss (someone or something you love)

recap: Faltam só dois dias para as férias! (There are only two days left until the holidays!)

intro: Entregar means to deliver, to hand in or to hand over. It's a regular -ar verb with a spelling change in eu entreguei, used for parcels, homework, keys and documents.

quick.en: Do you deliver to your home?

presente.en: I'm handing in the report on Friday.
Are you giving the key to the landlord?

presente.pt: O carteiro [entrega] o correio de manhã.
presente.en: The postman delivers the mail in the morning.
We deliver the orders to your home.
They deliver pizzas until midnight.

perfeito.en: I've already handed in the assignment to the teacher.
Did you hand in the documents?
The courier delivered the parcel yesterday.
We handed the keys to the landlord.

imperfeito.en: I used to deliver newspapers when I was young.

imperfeito.pt: O carteiro [entregava] sempre o correio às dez.
imperfeito.en: The postman always delivered the mail at ten.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [entregávamos] os trabalhos sempre a tempo.
imperfeito.en: We always handed in our work on time.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [entregavam] o pão de manhã cedo.
imperfeito.en: They used to deliver the bread early in the morning.

futuro.en: I will hand in the report tomorrow.

futuro.pt: A loja [entregará] o sofá na segunda.
futuro.en: The shop will deliver the sofa on Monday.
We will deliver everything on time.

futuro.pt: Eles [entregarão] as chaves no fim do mês.
futuro.en: They will hand over the keys at the end of the month.

condicional.pt: Eu [entregaria] o trabalho hoje, mas não está pronto.
condicional.en: I would hand in the work today, but it isn't ready.
Would you give this to João?

condicional.pt: A loja [entregaria] amanhã, mas é feriado.
condicional.en: The shop would deliver tomorrow, but it's a public holiday.

condicional.pt: Eles [entregariam] em casa por cinco euros.
condicional.en: They would deliver to your home for five euros.

presente.en: The postman delivers the mail in the morning.
presente.pt: O carteiro entrega o correio de manhã.

presente.en: Do you deliver to people's homes?
I'm handing in the report on Friday.

perfeito.en: I've already handed in my homework.
perfeito.pt: Já entreguei os trabalhos de casa.

perfeito.en: Did you hand in the keys?
They delivered the sofa yesterday.

imperfeito.en: I used to deliver newspapers.
He always handed in his work late.
imperfeito.pt: Ele entregava sempre os trabalhos tarde.

imperfeito.en: They delivered bread every morning.
imperfeito.pt: Eles entregavam pão todas as manhãs.

futuro.en: I'm going to hand in the report tomorrow.
When are they going to deliver the parcel?
We are going to deliver everything on time.

condicional.en: I would hand it in today.
Would you give this to Ana?
They would deliver on Monday.

notes.presente: Entregar algo a alguém = to hand something to someone. A entrega = the delivery; entregar ao domicílio = to deliver to your home. The presente often covers near-future plans: entrego na sexta.
notes.perfeito: Spelling change: g becomes gu before e, so eu entreguei (keeps the hard g). Also note European entregámos.
notes.imperfeito: Entregava describes a habit: Eu entregava jornais (I used to deliver newspapers).
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vou entregar o relatório amanhã.

compare.ex: Dei um presente à minha mãe.
Levo o bolo para a festa.

recap: Entreguei o relatório a tempo e fui jantar fora. (I handed in the report on time and went out for dinner.)

intro: Casar means to marry or to get married. It's a regular -ar verb; you marry someone with com: casar com alguém. Casar and casar-se are both correct.

quick.en: She got married in the summer.

presente.en: I'm getting married in June!
When are you getting married?
My sister is getting married on Saturday.
We're getting married in the village church.
Many couples get married in the summer.

perfeito.en: I got married ten years ago.
He married a Portuguese woman.
We got married in Lisbon.
My parents got married very young.

intro: Pegar means to take hold of, to pick up or to grab. It's a regular -ar verb (eu peguei), and in Portugal it is usually followed by em: pegar no saco, pegar nas chaves.

notes.presente: In Portugal pegar is normally followed by em: pegar no saco, pegar na mala, pegar nisto (em + o = no, em + a = na, em + isto = nisto). For buses and trains Portugal uses apanhar: apanhar o autocarro (Brazil: pegar o ônibus).
notes.perfeito: Spelling change: g becomes gu before e, so eu peguei (keeps the hard g). Also European pegámos. Pegar can also mean to catch on: a moda pegou.
notes.imperfeito: Pegava describes a habit: o meu avô pegava sempre no jornal (my grandfather always used to pick up the paper).
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vou pegar nas caixas.

patterns.en: to pick up in your arms

intro: Apontar means to point or to aim, and in Portugal it also means to write down or jot down. It's a regular -ar verb: apontar para a porta, apontar o número.

presente.en: I write everything down in a notebook.
Will you write down the number?

notes.presente: Apontar para = to point at / towards: aponta para a porta. In Portugal apontar also means to write down: aponta o meu número. Os apontamentos = notes (from a class); tirar apontamentos = to take notes.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: apontámos (Brazil: apontamos). Apontar can also mean to point out a mistake or problem: apontaram vários erros.
notes.imperfeito: Apontava describes a habit or an ongoing action: a criança apontava para tudo.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vou apontar a data.

patterns.en: to write down the number / address

intro: Virar means to turn or to flip. It's a regular -ar verb you'll need for directions (vira à direita), for cooking (virar o bife) and for turning around (virar-se).

presente.en: I turn left at the traffic lights.

presente.pt: Eles [viram] a mesa para a janela.

perfeito.en: I turned right at the roundabout.

notes.imperfeito: Use the imperfeito to describe how a road or path went: o caminho virava à esquerda.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vais virar à direita. O tempo vai virar = the weather is going to change.

patterns.en: to turn upside down / inside out

intro: Concluir means to conclude, to finish or to complete. It's an -uir verb, so some forms differ from regular -ir verbs (tu concluis, ele conclui) and several take an accent (concluímos, concluí). It's a bit formal; you'll hear it about courses, projects and conclusions.

presente.en: I finish my course in June.
What do you conclude from this?

presente.pt: O médico [conclui] que não é grave.
presente.en: The doctor concludes that it isn't serious.

presente.pt: Os estudantes [concluem] o mestrado este ano.

perfeito.en: I finished my degree in 2020.

notes.presente: Concluir follows the -uir pattern, like incluir, contribuir and distribuir: tu concluis and ele conclui end in -is / -i (not -es / -e), and nós concluímos takes an accent to keep the i stressed.
notes.perfeito: Accents mark the stressed í: concluí, concluíste, concluímos, concluíram (but concluiu has none). Nós concluímos is the same in the presente and the perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: The imperfeito keeps the accent on every form: concluía, concluías, concluíamos, concluíam.
notes.futuro: Concluir sounds formal. In everyday speech you'll more often hear acabar or terminar with ir + infinitivo: vou acabar o curso.

intro: Obrigar means to force, to oblige or to make someone do something: obrigar alguém a + infinitivo. It's a regular -ar verb (eu obriguei), and it's where obrigado (thank you) comes from.

notes.presente: Obrigar alguém a + infinitivo = to make / force someone to do something: obrigam-me a estudar. Ser obrigado a = to be forced to. Obrigado / obrigada (thank you) comes from this verb: literally '(I am) obliged'.
notes.perfeito: Spelling change: g becomes gu before e, so eu obriguei (keeps the hard g). Also European obrigámos.
notes.imperfeito: Obrigava describes what someone used to make you do: os meus pais obrigavam-me a comer legumes.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, ninguém te vai obrigar. After não, nunca, ninguém the pronoun goes before the verb.

notes.presente: Preparar works for food (preparar o jantar), trips (preparar as malas) and events. Preparar-se para = to get ready for: preparo-me para o exame. Estar preparado/a = to be ready.

notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vou preparar o jantar. With the reflexive: vais preparar-te para o exame?

intro: Desejar means to wish or to desire. It's a regular -ar verb, more formal than querer; you'll hear it from waiters (Deseja mais alguma coisa?) and in good wishes (Desejo-te boa sorte!).

quick.en: I wish you all the best!

perfeito.pt: Ele [desejou]-nos um bom fim de semana.
perfeito.en: He wished us a good weekend.
Everyone wished me luck.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I wanted to be an astronaut.
She really wanted a dog.

notes.presente: Desejar is more formal than querer. Shop and restaurant staff use it all the time with você / o senhor / a senhora: O que deseja? / Deseja mais alguma coisa? To wish someone something: desejar algo a alguém, desejo-te boa sorte.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: desejámos (Brazil: desejamos). With todos as subject the pronoun usually goes before the verb: Todos me desejaram boa sorte.
notes.imperfeito: Desejava can be a past wish (desejava ser astronauta) or, in speech, a polite request: Desejava uma mesa para dois, por favor.
notes.futuro: The synthetic future of desejar is rare in speech; use ir + infinitivo: vou desejar-lhe boa sorte.

recap: Desejo-te uma boa viagem e tudo de bom! (I wish you a good trip and all the best!)

intro: Imaginar means to imagine, to picture or to suppose. It's a regular -ar verb, and it gives you very common expressions like Nem imaginas! (You have no idea!) and Imagino que sim (I suppose so).

notes.presente: Imaginar takes an infinitive or que: imagino que sim (I suppose so), imagino viver aqui. Nem imaginas! (You have no idea!) is extremely common in Portugal.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: imaginámos (Brazil: imaginamos). After nunca and ninguém there's no change to the verb: nunca imaginei, ninguém imaginou.
notes.imperfeito: The imperfeito is perfect for past expectations: Eu imaginava Lisboa mais pequena (I'd pictured Lisbon smaller). Note ia ser = was going to be.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, não vais imaginar o que aconteceu!

compare.ex: Sonho com uma casa no campo.

recap: Nunca imaginei que ia gostar tanto de Lisboa! (I never imagined I would like Lisbon so much!)

intro: Discutir means both to argue and to discuss. It's a regular -ir verb: discutir com alguém is usually an argument, discutir um assunto is a discussion.

notes.presente: Discutir covers both meanings: discutir com alguém = to argue with someone; discutir um assunto = to discuss a topic. For a calm conversation, falar sobre is also common. Estar sempre a discutir = to be always arguing.
notes.perfeito: In -ir verbs, nós is the same in the presente and the perfeito: discutimos = we argue / we argued. Discutir por causa de = to argue about.
notes.imperfeito: Discutiam muito = they used to argue a lot (a repeated situation). Discutiram = they had an argument (one time).
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vamos discutir isso amanhã.

compare.ex: Vamos debater o tema na aula.

recap: Discutimos muito, mas fazemos sempre as pazes. (We argue a lot, but we always make up.)

intro: Preferir means to prefer. It has a stem change in the eu form of the presente (prefiro); the other forms are regular. You prefer one thing to another with a: prefiro chá a café.

notes.presente: Stem change in eu only: prefiro (e becomes i); the rest keep the e: preferes, prefere, preferimos. Preferir X a Y = to prefer X to Y: prefiro o verão ao inverno. You'll hear 'prefiro X do que Y' in speech, but a is the correct form.
notes.perfeito: The perfeito is regular: preferi, preferiste, preferiu. Nós preferimos is the same in the presente and the perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: In European Portuguese the imperfeito often replaces the condicional to sound polite or softer: Eu preferia ficar em casa = I'd rather stay at home.
notes.futuro: Everyday alternative: ir + infinitivo, vais preferir o novo.

compare.ex: Gosto mais de chá do que de café.

recap: Prefiro o comboio ao avião: é mais calmo. (I prefer the train to the plane: it's calmer.)
